cvEn:
Mordehai (Motke) Topel, son of Basha and David, was born on 3 Adar II 5689 (15 March 1929) in the town of Ostrowiec, Poland. In March 1936 he arrived in the country with his parents, who settled in Tel Aviv. He studied at a high school. From a young age he was a member of the Haganah.

To earn a living he distributed the newspaper "Maariv," but his dream was to become a geological engineer so that he could discover oil sources in the Negev. He went to the United States, studied there for about a year, and returned to the country at the start of the War of Independence to serve as a pilot. Mordehai served from the beginning of the war. So as not to lose the family's source of income, he would sell his newspapers every afternoon and then get to the airfield in time to fly. He served as a dispatcher on flights supplying besieged settlements, dropping ammunition and food to them. When the roads were cut off he flew to Haifa, and during the fighting at Castel he flew to Jerusalem.

Mordehai fell on 6 Iyar 5708 (15 May 1948), while defending the Tel Aviv airfield, which was bombed that day. He was laid to rest in the Nahalat Yitzhak military cemetery. In his memory the song "Shir Zikaron LeGibor Yisrael" ("A Memorial Song for a Hero of Israel") was composed, with lyrics by Yigal Carmi and music by Gabriel Gerad.
